units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 2:5">Targ. O. Gen. II, 5</cite> <cite ref="L00533"><he>לַיִת</he></cite> (some ed. <cite ref="L00533"><he>לַיָת</he></cite>; Y. <cite ref="L00458"><he>לַיִית</he></cite>). Ib. XLVII, 13 <cite ref="L00533"><he>לֵית</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 25:14">Targ. Prov. XXV, 14</cite> <cite ref="L00020"><he>לָאִית</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 38:4">Targ. Ps. XXXVIII, 4</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 4a:11">B. Mets. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>למלוה אית … ללוה ל׳ וכ׳</he> the creditor has witnesses, the debtor has none.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 5a:16">Ib. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>השתא נמי דליתא לדר׳ חייא</he> now, likewise, when R. Ḥiya’s opinion is not adopted.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 5a:13">Ib.</cite> <he>מודה … לית ליה</he> he does not hold the opinion that the admission of the defendent must be of the nature of the claim; a. v. fr.—With suffix: <he>לֵיתֵנָא</he> I (am) not; <he>לֵיתָךְ</he>, <he>לָיְתָךְ</he>, <cite ref="L00515"><he>לַיְי׳</he></cite> thou (art) not; <he>לֵיתיֹהִי</he>, <he>לָיְ׳</he> he (is) not (no more) &c.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 32:1">Targ. Y. I Deut. XXXII, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 39:9">Ib. XXXIX, 9</cite> (Y. <he>לַיְתֵיה</he>) there is none. Ib. XXXI, 2; 5 <he>לֵיתַנּוּן</he> ed. Berl. (ed. <he>לֵיתָנוּן</he>, <he>לֵיתַנִין</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 59:14">Targ. Ps. LIX, 14</cite> <he>לֵיתִינוּן</he> ed. Lag. (ed. Wil. <he>לֵיתִנוּן</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Esther 3:8">Targ. Esth. III, 8</cite> <he>לֵיתְהוֹן</he>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shevuot 48a:11">Shebu. 48ᵃ</cite> <he>אי אִיתָהּ … איתה אי לֵיתָהּ ליתה</he> if the opinion of … is to be adopted, it must be applied in each case; if rejected, in neither.
<cite ref="Ketubot 22a:2">Keth. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>וחד ליתוהי</he> and one (of us judges) is no more.
<cite ref="Shevuot 14b:12">Shebu. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>דלֵיתַנְהוּ בכל וכ׳</he> (not … <he>הי</he>) which do not occur in the Torah, opp. <he>דאיתנהו</he>; a. fr.
